title: The Mixtape of the band room
premise: Oscar Sandoval, a scholarship senior at Wexford Preparatory Academy, has survived three years by being agreeable, useful, and silent — especially about the hazing culture festering in the school's elite music program, which his best friend Theo quietly runs. When the college essay prompt asks students to describe a moment they failed to act, Oscar's honest draft accidentally circulates through the band room, exposing secrets Theo and the administration would rather bury. As Oscar is pressured to recant, they must choose between the belonging they've craved and the truth that could free everyone — including Theo, whose complicity hides his own victimhood. In the end, Oscar reads the essay aloud at graduation rehearsal, losing the friendship but sparking an investigation that finally lets them belong to themselves.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is a former high school orchestra librarian who spent a decade collecting the confessions students whispered between sheet-music shelves. She writes from a coastal town in Maine, where she keeps every mixtape she's ever been given.

chapters.title: The Question on Page One
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Senior year begins and the common app essay prompt — 'describe a time you failed to act' — lands in Oscar's lap like an accusation. They draft three safe, lying versions and delete them all. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as ambition, establishing Oscar's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Second Chair, First Rule
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In band room flashbacks and present-day rehearsals, we learn the rules of Wexford's music program: don't question the section leaders, don't touch the trophy case, don't be the scholarship kid who complains. Emotional beat: the suffocating comfort of belonging at a price.

chapters.title: Theo's Mixtape
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo curates a mixtape for the band room's ancient boombox, a tradition he inherited from the seniors who once tormented him. He tells himself the rituals he now enforces are gentler than what he endured. Emotional beat: complicity rationalized as mercy.

chapters.title: The Draft That Told the Truth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At 2 a.m., Oscar writes a fourth draft — honest, furious, naming the hazing without naming names — and saves it to the shared drive meant for essay swaps with their writing group. Emotional beat: the dangerous relief of finally saying it.

chapters.title: Circulation
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, Oscar's writing-group partner, forwards the draft to one friend 'for feedback only.' By lunch it's in every group chat in the school. Emotional beat: horror spreading at the speed of a screenshot.

chapters.title: What the Band Room Heard
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs — freshmen, section leaders, the drum major. Each reader sees themselves in the essay, some as victims, some as perpetrators, some as both. Emotional beat: the essay becomes a mirror no one can look away from.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Theo confronts Oscar privately, hurt and cold: fix this, deny it, or the scholarship committee hears about 'attitude problems.' Oscar realizes their safest friend has become the threat. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Dean's Office Smells Like Lemon Polish
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Dean Whitlock offers a deal — recant, and Wexford will 'protect' Oscar's college prospects. The administration's concern is reputation, not students. Emotional beat: power's soft voice and hard hands.

chapters.title: Priya's Apology, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confesses the forward to Oscar, who can't decide whether to be angry or grateful — the leak did what silence never could. Their friendship strains and re-forms around the truth. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Freshman Who Quit
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. A first-year tuba player, emboldened by the circulating essay, quits the program and tells his parents everything. His complaint lands on Whitlock's desk the same week Oscar's does. Emotional beat: one small courage making others possible.

chapters.title: Mixtape, Track Two
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo plays a song from the year he was hazed and remembers his older brother telling him to 'survive it, then run it better.' We see how power was handed to him like a poisoned inheritance. Emotional beat: grief for who he was supposed to become.

chapters.title: The Recantation Draft
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Under pressure, Oscar writes a public retraction — and can't finish it. Every sentence feels like swallowing glass. They leave the document blank except for one line: 'I meant all of it.' Emotional beat: the cost of honesty priced in full.

chapters.title: Locked Band Room
chapters.summary: Oscar and Theo, alternating POVs. Trapped together after hours by a broken door, they finally say the unsayable: Theo was hazed too, Oscar knew and said nothing, and both of them protected the system to survive it. Emotional beat: raw, exhausted honesty between people who can't afford to lose each other.

chapters.title: The Committee
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Wexford convenes a 'climate review' that is transparently a containment operation. Oscar is asked to testify anonymously — anonymity that protects the school more than the students. Emotional beat: watching institutions perform accountability.

chapters.title: Everything Priya Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reveals she's been archiving screenshots, emails, and recordings for months — her own quiet failure to act, now weaponized for good. She offers the archive to Oscar. Emotional beat: guilt converted into ammunition.

chapters.title: The Offer Oscar Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Whitlock escalates: a full scholarship renewal contingent on silence, plus a glowing letter — the future Oscar's family has sacrificed for, traded for one essay. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable and most corrupt.

chapters.title: What Oscar's Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar's mother, a school custodian at Wexford for twelve years, reveals she has seen everything — the hazing, the cover-ups — and stayed silent to keep her job and Oscar's enrollment. Emotional beat: inherited silence, and the choice to break it together.

chapters.title: Track Thirteen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo anonymously submits his own account to the review committee, then deletes his mixtape playlist from the boombox — ending the tradition. He and Oscar don't reconcile, but he stops fighting the investigation. Emotional beat: a friendship ending honestly instead of falsely continuing.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't a Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya sends the full archive — including Whitlock's 'protection' offer in writing — to the school board and a local journalist. The story breaks the week of graduation rehearsals. Emotional beat: the point of no return, crossed on purpose.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End of the World
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At graduation rehearsal, with the school in chaos, Oscar takes the podium during open remarks and reads the original essay aloud, unedited, naming the system rather than the people. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice — the climax.

chapters.title: The Sound After
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Silence, then scattered applause, then the board's announcement of an independent investigation; Whitlock resigns; Marcus re-enlists in the band on his own terms. Oscar's scholarship is uncertain but their integrity isn't. Emotional beat: consequences arriving, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Oscar's College Essay (Final Draft)
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epistolary. Oscar submits a revised essay — not about failing to act, but about the day they finally did — and mails a copy of Theo's old mixtape to their dorm-bound self, a promise to never again mistake silence for safety. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, to oneself.
